title: Banner Replacement, Shop Toggle Fix, Admin Redesign & Delivery Logic

requirements.summary: Replace all vegetable/sabji-themed banners with professional general grocery banners showcasing Rice, Oil, Biscuits, and Snacks
acceptanceCriteria: No vegetable or sabji images appear anywhere on the homepage
HeroBannerCarousel displays at least 2 banners featuring Rice, Oil, Biscuits, or Snacks themes
New banners look professional and match a general grocery store aesthetic

file_operations.description: Replace the existing banner image paths with the newly generated grocery banners. Update the images array to reference frontend/public/assets/generated/grocery-banner-rice-oil.dim_1200x400.png and frontend/public/assets/generated/grocery-banner-biscuits-snacks.dim_1200x400.png. Remove any references to vegetable or sabji-themed images.

requirements.summary: Rewrite ShopStatusToggle component to directly call backend mutation and optimistically update UI, enforcing shop-closed restrictions across ProductCard and CartDrawer
acceptanceCriteria: Toggling to 'Closed' in the admin panel immediately persists the closed state to the backend
ShopClosedBanner appears on the homepage without requiring a page reload after closing
All 'Add to Cart' buttons are visually disabled and non-functional when shop is closed
CartDrawer prevents navigation to checkout when shop is closed
Toggling back to 'Open' re-enables all Add to Cart buttons and hides the closed banner immediately

file_operations.description: Delete all existing code in this file and rewrite the component from scratch. Use the useSetShopStatus mutation from useQueries.ts to toggle shop status. Implement optimistic UI updates using queryClient.setQueryData to immediately update the ['shopStatus'] query cache when the toggle is clicked. Display loading and pending states during the mutation. On success, the mutation should automatically invalidate the shopStatus query to ensure consistency. On error, revert the optimistic update and display an error message.

Update the ProductCard component to accept isShopClosed as a prop. When isShopClosed is true, disable all 'Add to Cart' buttons and apply visual styling (opacity reduction, cursor-not-allowed) to indicate they are disabled. Prevent the handleAddToCart function from executing when the shop is closed. Ensure the 'Delivery in 10 Mins' badge remains visible regardless of shop status.

Ensure the ProductGrid fetches the current shop status using the useGetShopStatus query from useQueries.ts and passes the isShopClosed boolean prop to every ProductCard component it renders. This ensures all product cards reflect the current shop status in real-time.

Update the CartDrawer to fetch the current shop status using useGetShopStatus. When the shop is closed (isShopClosed === true), disable the 'Proceed to Checkout' button and display a warning message indicating the shop is currently closed. Prevent navigation to the checkout page when the button is clicked if the shop is closed. The cart items and quantity controls should remain functional for browsing purposes.

Ensure the ShopClosedBanner fetches the shop status using useGetShopStatus and only renders the banner when isShopClosed is true and the query has successfully fetched (isFetched is true). This ensures the banner appears and disappears immediately when the shop status changes without requiring a page reload.
Verify that the HomePage renders the ShopClosedBanner component so it appears on the homepage when the shop is closed. Ensure the banner is positioned prominently above the ProductGrid.

requirements.summary: Redesign AdminPage with a dark/blue dashboard theme featuring clean metric cards for Total Orders, Active Users, and Shop Status
acceptanceCriteria: Admin panel uses a dark navy/slate background with blue accent colors
Three stat cards are visible at the top: Total Orders, Active Users, Shop Status
Each stat card displays a live value fetched from the backend
Shop Status card shows green when open and red when closed
All tabs (Orders, Products, Settings, Bills) are restyled to match the dark/blue theme
Admin panel looks professional and clean on both desktop and mobile

file_operations.description: Redesign the AdminPage layout with a dark navy/slate background color (e.g., bg-slate-900 or bg-navy-950). Add a stats overview row at the top of the page containing three metric cards: (1) Total Orders displaying the count from useGetAllOrders, (2) Active Users displaying the distinct count of users with orders (calculate from orders data by counting unique customer names or principals), and (3) Shop Status displaying the current open/closed state from useGetShopStatus with a green indicator when open and red when closed. Style each card with a dark background (bg-slate-800), rounded corners, padding, and white/light text. Apply blue accent colors (e.g., text-blue-400, border-blue-500) to the tab navigation. Ensure the existing tabs (Orders, Products, Settings, Bills) are restyled to match the dark/blue theme with hover states and active tab highlighting. Maintain responsive layout for mobile.

requirements.summary: Ensure 'Delivery in 10 Mins' badge is rendered on every ProductCard and verify free delivery threshold logic in CartDrawer and CheckoutPage
acceptanceCriteria: 'Delivery in 10 Mins' badge is visible on every product card in the grid
Cart total below ₹51 shows a ₹5 delivery charge
Cart total of ₹51 or above shows free delivery (₹0 delivery charge)
Delivery fee dynamically updates as items are added or removed from cart
CheckoutPage order summary reflects the correct delivery fee

file_operations.description: Verify that the ProductCard component renders a 'Delivery in 10 Mins' badge (e.g., a small badge with green background and white text) prominently on every product card, positioned near the product image or price. Ensure the badge is always visible regardless of shop status or product availability.

Update the CartDrawer to calculate and display the delivery fee based on the free delivery threshold logic: if the cart subtotal is ₹51 or above, display ₹0 delivery fee (free delivery); if the cart subtotal is below ₹51 and the distance is within 1km, display a ₹5 delivery fee. Since distance is not available in the CartDrawer context, assume 1km for the ₹5 charge. Display the delivery fee as a separate line item in the cart total breakdown (Subtotal, Delivery Fee, Total). Ensure the delivery fee updates dynamically as items are added or removed.

Update the CheckoutPage order summary section to calculate and display the delivery fee using the same logic as CartDrawer: ₹0 for orders ₹51 and above, ₹5 for orders below ₹51 (assuming 1km distance). Display the breakdown as Subtotal, Delivery Fee, and Total. Ensure the delivery fee is included in the total amount passed to the placeOrder backend call. Note: The backend's calculateTotalPrice method already handles this logic based on distanceInKm, so ensure the frontend displays the fee correctly before order placement.
